unit.title: Provide basic manicure and pedicure service

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the consultation before a manicure?
options: To find the client's wishes and check the hands for problems
To sell the client as many polish colours as possible
To decide which music the client would like to hear
To check how long the client's nails have been growing

questions.stem: Which of these means you should not give a manicure, and should refer the client to a doctor?
options: Dry cuticles and a few hangnails
Short nails that have been bitten
Red, swollen, painful skin with pus around a nail
Nails stained a little yellow from wearing dark polish for weeks

questions.stem: A client has thick, yellow, crumbly toenails that may be a fungal infection. What should you do?
options: File the nails down hard and paint over them
Do not treat those nails, and advise her to see a doctor
Soak the feet for longer to soften the infection
Use the same file on all ten nails, then on the next client

questions.stem: Why must you take extra care with a pedicure client who has diabetes?
options: Diabetes makes the nails grow much faster than normal
Clients with diabetes are not allowed to wear nail polish
Diabetes makes the skin on the feet thicker and harder to cut
Small cuts on the feet may heal slowly and become infected

questions.stem: A client has a wart on one finger. What should you do?
options: Cut the wart off carefully with cuticle nippers
File the wart down until it is flat with the skin
Avoid touching it, as warts spread, and refer the client
Massage warm oil into the wart to soften it first

questions.stem: Which tool is used to push back the cuticle gently?
options: A cuticle pusher or a wrapped orange stick
Cuticle nippers, pressed flat against the nail plate
Toenail clippers
A foot file

questions.stem: What are cuticle nippers used for?
options: Cutting the live cuticle right back to the skin
Trimming hangnails and loose dead skin only
Shaping the free edge of the toenails
Pushing back the cuticle after soaking

questions.stem: What should you do with an emery board (nail file) after it has been used on a client?
options: Rinse it under the tap and use it on the next client
Keep it in the drawer for that client's next visit if it is still rough
Spray it with perfume to freshen it
Throw it away, or give it to the client, because it is single-use

questions.stem: What is the correct order for making metal tools safe between clients?
options: Disinfect them first, then wash off the disinfectant with tap water
Wipe them with a towel and put them away
Store them in the drawer and clean them weekly
Clean off dirt with soap and water, then disinfect or sterilise

questions.stem: How should a foot spa or pedicure bowl be treated after each client?
options: Rinse it with cold water and leave it full for the next client
Drain, clean and disinfect it as the maker's instructions say
Add more water and a few drops of perfume
Wipe the outside only, because the inside is wet anyway

questions.stem: Where should a used blade or other sharp item go?
options: In the general rubbish bin
In a plastic bag on the trolley
In a sharps box
Back in the tool drawer

questions.stem: Why does the nail technician wash her hands before and after each client?
options: To stop germs passing between clients and herself
To make the polish dry faster on the nails
Because it softens her own cuticles
To remove the smell of nail polish remover from her skin

questions.stem: Which nail shape has straight sides and a straight free edge with sharp corners?
options: Square
Oval
Round
Pointed

questions.stem: How should you file natural fingernails?
options: With a fast sawing action back and forth
With a metal file pressed hard into the corners
From the centre outwards, pressing down on the nail plate
From each side towards the centre, in one direction

questions.stem: How should toenails be cut to help prevent ingrown toenails?
options: Into a deep curve that goes down at the corners
Into sharp points at the sides
Straight across, level with the end of the toe
As short as possible, below the skin

questions.stem: What does a cuticle remover or softener do?
options: Makes the nail plate grow faster
Softens dead cuticle skin so it can be eased off the nail
Dries the polish faster
Hardens the cuticle so that it stops growing over the nail plate

questions.stem: Why do you remove old polish before starting a manicure?
options: Because old polish makes the nails grow faster
So you can see the nails and skin and check for problems
Because clients will not pay for nails that still have old polish
To give the remover time to soften the cuticles

questions.stem: How should you remove dark polish without staining the skin?
options: Rub the soaked pad round and round over the nail, cuticle and skin
Scrape the polish off with an orange stick
Press a soaked pad on the nail for a moment, then wipe from cuticle to tip
Soak the whole hand in remover for five minutes

questions.stem: What is the usual order for applying nail polish?
options: Top coat, colour, then base coat
Colour, base coat, then top coat
One thick coat of colour with no base coat or top coat
Base coat, two thin coats of colour, then top coat

questions.stem: Why is a base coat applied before coloured polish?
options: It protects the nail from stains and helps the polish stick
It makes the colour dry darker
It removes the natural oils from the skin around the nail
It softens the cuticle so that it is easier to push back later

questions.stem: Why must the nail plate be clean and free of oil before polish?
options: So that the polish smells better
So that the polish dries to a darker, richer shade
So that the polish sticks and does not peel
So that the nail grows faster under it

questions.stem: Which massage movement is a smooth stroking used at the start of a hand massage?
options: Petrissage
Effleurage
Tapotement
Vibration

questions.stem: Why is a hand and arm massage included in a manicure?
options: It relaxes the client and helps blood flow
It makes the nails change shape
It removes polish stains
It cures stiff joints and arthritis for good

questions.stem: When should you NOT massage a client's feet?
options: When the client's feet are tired after a long day at work
When the skin is dry but unbroken
When the client likes firm pressure
When there are cuts, swelling or signs of infection

questions.stem: What is a pumice stone or foot file used for in a pedicure?
options: To shape the toenails
To push back the cuticles on each toe
To apply polish to the toenails
To smooth hard skin on the soles

questions.stem: Why is a pumice or foot file used, rather than a blade, to smooth hard skin in a basic pedicure?
options: A blade can cut the skin and let in infection
A blade makes the skin grow back softer
A file takes much longer, so the client pays more
A blade cannot remove any hard skin at all

questions.stem: What should be done to the feet before a pedicure starts?
options: Apply polish to see which colour suits
Check them for problems and cleanse them
Cut the toenails as short as possible
Massage them with a strong cream

questions.stem: After soaking, why do you dry the feet well, especially between the toes?
options: So that the polish colour looks brighter
So that the client's shoes fit better
To help prevent fungal infections such as athlete's foot
So that the toenails can be cut much more easily and quickly

questions.stem: What is athlete's foot?
options: A bruise on the big toe from sport
A fungal infection of the skin, often between the toes
Hard, cracked skin on the heel that forms from running in sport
An allergy to nail polish

questions.stem: Why must nail polish and remover be kept away from heat and flames?
options: They will turn a different colour
They will become too thick and stringy to use
They will lose their smell
They are flammable and can catch fire

questions.stem: Why should a nail station be well ventilated?
options: To keep the polish cold
To dry the client's hands and nails faster after soaking
To carry away fumes from polish and remover
To stop the files from wearing out

questions.stem: What should you do if nail polish remover splashes into a client's eye?
options: Rinse the eye with plenty of clean, cool water and get help
Wipe the eye with a cotton pad soaked in remover
Tell the client to blink a few times, then carry on with the service
Cover the eye with a dry towel and wait

questions.stem: How should the manicure station be set up?
options: Clean, with disinfected tools and fresh towels ready
With tools from the last client left out to save time
With all products open so they are ready
With the used towels folded for reuse

questions.stem: How should the client be seated for a pedicure?
options: On a stool with no back, feet on the floor
Standing, with one foot on a chair
In a comfortable chair, with the feet supported
Lying flat on a towel on the floor with the feet raised

questions.stem: White spots on a nail plate, often from a small knock, are called what?
options: Onychomycosis
Paronychia
Pterygium
Leuconychia

questions.stem: Before a warm paraffin wax hand treatment, how do you check that the wax is safe?
options: Ask the client to dip one finger in first
Test it on the inside of your own wrist
Check that it is bubbling hot
Wait until it has gone fully hard

questions.stem: How do you avoid air bubbles in nail polish?
options: Shake the bottle hard before use
Blow on each coat to dry it faster
Roll the bottle gently between your hands
Apply one very thick coat instead of two thin ones

questions.stem: Which aftercare advice should you give after a manicure?
options: Soak the hands in hot water as soon as you get home
Use the nails as tools to open cans
Pick at the cuticles to keep them short
Wear gloves for washing up and use hand cream daily

questions.stem: Which footwear advice helps prevent ingrown toenails?
options: Wear shoes a size smaller so that the foot is held firmly
Wear shoes that fit well and do not squeeze the toes
Wear plastic shoes with no air holes
Go barefoot in public showers

questions.stem: Why do you keep a record card for each manicure and pedicure client?
options: To share the client's details with other salons nearby
To track how much the client tips
To decide whether to raise her prices
To note health details, treatments and any reactions

questions.stem: Why are metal tools kept in a closed container after disinfecting?
options: So they do not rust in the air
To stop the clients from seeing the sharp tools
So that they stay warm for the client
To keep them clean until they are used

questions.stem: Which step comes first in a basic manicure, after the consultation?
options: Apply the base coat
Remove old polish and check the nails
Massage the client's hands and lower arms
Push back the cuticles

questions.stem: Which question best helps you choose the nail shape and length?
options: What do you do in your free time on weekends?
How much did your last manicure cost?
What work do you do with your hands each day?
Which colour is your favourite?

questions.stem: What should you do with a towel used on a client's feet?
options: Put it in the laundry and use a fresh one for the next client
Use it to dry the same client's hands and then the next client's feet
Shake it out and fold it for the next client
Hang it on the chair to dry for later

questions.stem: How do you check the finished polish before the client leaves?
options: Look for smudges, bubbles and polish on the skin
Press each nail hard to test if it is dry
Blow hard on the nails
Ask the client to put her shoes on quickly

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the thin layer of dead skin on the nail plate, near its base, that is gently pushed back?
Name the nail shape with straight sides and a curved tip like the end of an egg.
What wooden stick, wrapped in cotton wool, is used to clean under the free edge?
What is the part of the nail that grows past the fingertip called?
What liquid is used to take off nail polish?

essays.stem: Describe how you carry out a consultation before a manicure or pedicure, and explain what contraindications you look for and what you do about them.
essays.modelAnswer: I greet the client, seat her comfortably and ask what she wants: nail shape, length and polish colour. I ask about her work and hobbies, her health, any allergies, and medical conditions such as diabetes or poor circulation, and about any medicines. Then I wash my hands and look closely at the hands or feet, nails and skin in good light. I look for contraindications: fungal infections such as athlete's foot or thick, yellow, crumbly nails; bacterial infection such as red, swollen skin with pus around the nail; warts; open cuts, bruising or swelling; and a nail that is lifting or very damaged. If there is an infection or open wound, I do not treat the area. I explain kindly, without trying to diagnose, and advise her to see a doctor. For a client with diabetes I take extra care and may ask for a doctor's advice first. I write everything on the record card and agree the plan and price.
markingPoints: Asks about wishes, lifestyle, health, allergies and medical conditions
Examines hands or feet, nails and skin in good light after washing hands
Names valid contraindications (fungal or bacterial infection, warts, cuts, swelling)
Does not treat infected areas; explains kindly and refers to a doctor
Records the consultation and agrees the plan

essays.stem: Explain how you prevent the spread of infection in manicure and pedicure services. Include tools, single-use items, sharps, towels and the foot spa.
essays.modelAnswer: Infection can pass from one client to another on tools, towels and water, so hygiene is part of every service. I wash my hands before and after each client and ask the client to wash or cleanse her hands or feet. Metal tools such as nippers and pushers are first cleaned with soap and water to remove dirt, then disinfected as the maker says, or sterilised in an autoclave where the Centre has one, and stored in a clean, closed container. Single-use items, such as emery boards, orange sticks, toe separators and buffers, are used once only, then thrown away or given to the client. Any blade or sharp item goes straight into a sharps box. I use fresh towels for each client and put used ones in a covered laundry bin. After each pedicure, the foot spa or bowl is drained, cleaned and disinfected as the maker's instructions say. I wipe the station with disinfectant between clients.
markingPoints: Hand washing before and after each client
Metal tools cleaned, then disinfected or sterilised, and stored closed
Single-use items used once only
Sharps into a sharps box; fresh towels for each client
Foot spa drained, cleaned and disinfected as the maker says

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how you carry out a basic manicure with polish.
essays.modelAnswer: After the consultation, I wash my hands and set out disinfected tools and fresh towels. I remove old polish by pressing a soaked pad on each nail and wiping from cuticle to tip. I check the nails again, then shape them with an emery board, filing from each side towards the centre in one direction. I put the fingers of one hand in a finger bowl of warm, soapy water, then dry them and apply cuticle softener. I gently push back the cuticle with a wrapped orange stick or cuticle pusher, and use nippers only for hangnails and loose dead skin. I clean under the free edge. I repeat with the other hand. I give a hand and arm massage using effleurage and petrissage. Then I remove all cream and oil from the nail plate. I apply a base coat, two thin coats of colour and a top coat, cleaning any polish off the skin. I check the result and give aftercare advice.
markingPoints: Preparation and removal of old polish
Shaping with correct filing technique
Soaking, cuticle softener and gentle cuticle work, nippers only for dead skin
Hand and arm massage
Nail plate cleaned of oil; base coat, two coats of colour, top coat; check and aftercare

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how you carry out a basic pedicure.
essays.modelAnswer: I seat the client comfortably with her feet supported and check the feet for contraindications such as athlete's foot, fungal nails, cuts or swelling. I wash my hands and put on gloves if the Centre's rules say so. I remove old polish and soak the feet in the clean foot spa or bowl of warm water with a foot soak, as the maker says. I dry the feet well, especially between the toes. I cut the toenails straight across with clean clippers, not too short, and file the edges smooth. I apply cuticle softener and push back the cuticles gently. I smooth hard skin on the heels and soles with a pumice stone or foot file, never a blade. I rinse and dry the feet again. I give a foot and lower leg massage with a cream, avoiding any broken skin. I remove cream from the toenails, put in toe separators, and apply base coat, two thin coats of colour and top coat. Finally I clean the foot spa and tools.
markingPoints: Comfortable seating and check of the feet for contraindications
Soak, then dry well between the toes
Toenails cut straight across and filed; cuticles pushed back gently
Hard skin smoothed with pumice or foot file, not a blade; foot massage
Nails cleaned and polished; foot spa and tools cleaned and disinfected

essays.stem: Describe four nail shapes and explain how to file natural nails correctly. Say how you would choose a shape for a client.
essays.modelAnswer: A square nail has straight sides and a straight free edge with sharp corners. It is strong, but the corners can catch. A round nail follows the shape of the fingertip and suits short nails and people who work with their hands. An oval nail has straight sides and a tip curved like the end of an egg, which makes fingers look longer. A squoval (square-oval) nail has a straight edge with softened, rounded corners, and is strong and popular. Pointed nails are narrow at the tip and break easily. To file natural nails, I hold the file at a slight angle under the free edge and file from each side towards the centre in one direction. I do not saw back and forth, because this splits the layers, and I do not file deep into the corners, which weakens the nail. To choose a shape, I look at the client's fingers, nail beds, lifestyle and work, and agree it with her.
markingPoints: Describes square and round correctly
Describes oval and squoval (or pointed) correctly
Files from each side to the centre in one direction
Avoids sawing and filing into the corners, and says why
Chooses the shape from fingers, lifestyle and the client's wishes

essays.stem: Explain how to apply nail polish to get a smooth, long-lasting finish, and what you do if the polish smudges.
essays.modelAnswer: First the nail plate must be clean and free of oil and cream, so I wipe each nail with polish remover. I roll the polish bottle gently between my hands instead of shaking it, so that no air bubbles form. I apply a base coat to protect the nail from stains and help the colour stick. Then I apply the colour in thin coats: usually one stroke down the centre and one down each side, from near the cuticle to the free edge, without flooding the cuticle. I let each coat dry a little before the next, and normally apply two thin coats. I seal the free edge by running the brush lightly along the tip. Last, I apply a top coat for shine and protection. I clean any polish off the skin with a wrapped orange stick dipped in remover. If a nail smudges while still wet, I gently remove the polish from that nail and reapply the coats, then check all nails again.
markingPoints: Nail plate cleaned of oil first; bottle rolled, not shaken
Base coat applied
Thin coats in a centre-and-sides pattern, two coats, free edge sealed
Top coat; polish cleaned off the skin
Smudge removed and the nail redone, then checked

essays.stem: Describe the massage movements used in a hand or foot massage, their benefits, and when you would not massage.
essays.modelAnswer: Effleurage is a smooth, stroking movement with the whole hand. It is used to begin and end the massage, to spread the cream and to link the other movements, and it is relaxing. Petrissage is a kneading movement that lifts, squeezes and presses the muscles. It eases tension and stiffness and helps blood flow. Friction is small, firm circles with the thumbs or fingertips, often used around the joints and on the soles. I keep an even rhythm and ask the client if the pressure is comfortable. Massage relaxes the client, warms the hands or feet, softens the skin with the cream and improves blood flow. I would not massage over cuts, bruising, swelling, varicose veins, recent fractures, or signs of infection such as athlete's foot or a red, hot area. I would ask a client with a medical condition, such as diabetes or a blood clot, to check with her doctor first.
markingPoints: Effleurage described and its use
Petrissage described and its use
Friction (or another correct movement) described, with even rhythm and comfortable pressure
Benefits: relaxation, warmth, blood flow, softer skin
Contraindications to massage and referral to a doctor where needed

essays.stem: Explain how to store and use nail products safely, and what first aid you give if a product gets into the eye or on the skin.
essays.modelAnswer: Many nail products, such as polish, remover and some cleansers, are flammable and give off fumes. I read the label and the safety data sheet, and follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules. I store products in their own labelled containers, with the lids tightly closed, in a cool, dry place away from heat, sunlight and flames, and out of the reach of children. I never put remover into an unlabelled bottle. At the station I keep only the amount I need and close each bottle after use. The area must be well ventilated so fumes are carried away, and nobody smokes nearby. I wipe up spills at once and put used cotton pads into a lined, covered bin. If a product splashes into an eye, I rinse it at once with plenty of clean, cool running water and get medical help. If it irritates the skin, I wash it off with water, stop the service and record the reaction.
markingPoints: Recognises products are flammable and give off fumes; follows label, SDS and rules
Stored labelled and closed, cool, away from heat and flames
Good ventilation, no smoking, minimum amounts at the station
Spills wiped at once; used pads in a covered bin
First aid: rinse eyes with clean water and get help; wash skin, stop and record

essays.stem: Explain why a client with diabetes needs extra care in a pedicure, and describe how you would change the service for her.
essays.modelAnswer: Diabetes can reduce the feeling in the feet and slow the blood flow to them. This means the client may not feel a cut, a burn or too much pressure, and small wounds can heal slowly and become badly infected. So I ask at the consultation whether she has diabetes, and I may ask her to check with her doctor before the service. I look carefully for cuts, sores, colour changes or swelling, and if I find any I do not treat that area and I refer her to a doctor. I test the water temperature carefully, because she may not feel heat, and keep the soak short. I do not cut the cuticles or use sharp tools near the skin, and I cut the nails straight across and file gently. I smooth hard skin only lightly with a foot file. I use gentle massage pressure. I record everything and advise her to check her feet every day and wear well-fitting shoes.
markingPoints: Diabetes reduces feeling and blood flow, so wounds heal slowly
Asks at consultation and may ask for a doctor's advice first
Checks for cuts, sores or swelling and refers instead of treating
Gentle changes: careful water temperature, no cutting near the skin, light filing and massage
Records and gives foot-care advice

essays.stem: Describe the aftercare advice you give after a manicure and a pedicure, and explain why you keep client records.
essays.modelAnswer: After a manicure, I advise the client to let the polish harden fully and to avoid hot water and heavy work for a while. I tell her to wear gloves for washing up, cleaning and gardening, to use hand cream and cuticle oil every day, and not to use her nails as tools or pick at the cuticles. I suggest she files any chips in one direction with an emery board and comes back regularly. After a pedicure, I advise wearing open shoes until the polish is dry, drying well between the toes after bathing, wearing shoes that fit and do not squeeze the toes, using foot cream on the heels but not between the toes, and checking the feet for problems. I tell her to contact a doctor if she sees redness, swelling or pain. On the record card I write the date, the consultation, any contraindications, the treatment, products and colours used, and any reaction. Records help plan the next visit and protect both the client and the salon.
markingPoints: Manicure aftercare: gloves, hand cream and cuticle oil, do not use nails as tools
Pedicure aftercare: dry between the toes, well-fitting shoes, foot cream
Advises seeing a doctor for redness, swelling or pain, and when to return
Records date, consultation, contraindications, products and reactions
Explains why records matter

practical1.title: Basic manicure with polish, given to a partner
practical1.brief: Work in pairs inside your group (one group of three if needed), in the Centre's salon, on members who agree to be clients. Each member gives a full basic manicure to a partner and receives one, so every member does every step while the assessor watches. Set up a clean station with disinfected tools and fresh towels. Carry out a consultation, check the hands and nails for contraindications and fill in a record card. Remove old polish, shape the nails, soak, apply cuticle softener and push back the cuticles gently, give a hand and arm massage, clean the nail plate and apply base coat, two thin coats of colour and a top coat. Throw away single-use items and clean, then disinfect, metal tools. Photograph each stage below, showing only hands and the work area.

Disinfected cuticle pushers and nippers in a closed container
New emery boards, orange sticks and cotton wool for each client
Polish remover, cuticle softener, hand cream, base coat, colours and top coat
Disinfectant made up as the maker says, and a sharps box

Applied base coat, two thin coats and top coat neatly, with no polish on the skin
Gave aftercare advice, threw away single-use items and cleaned, then disinfected, the tools

Keep polish and remover closed, away from heat and flames, in a ventilated area

Rinse eyes with clean, cool water if a product splashes, and report it

practical2.title: Basic pedicure with foot spa care, given to a partner
practical2.brief: Work in pairs inside your group (one group of three if needed), in the Centre's salon, on members who agree to be clients. Each member gives a basic pedicure to a partner and receives one, so every member does every step while the assessor watches. Seat the client comfortably with the feet supported. Consult, check the feet for contraindications such as athlete's foot, fungal nails or cuts, and fill in a record card. Soak the feet, dry them well between the toes, cut the toenails straight across and file them, push back the cuticles, smooth hard skin with a pumice stone or foot file (no blades), give a foot and lower leg massage and apply polish with toe separators. At the end each member drains, cleans and disinfects the foot spa or bowl as the maker says. Photos show only feet, hands and the work area.

Foot spa or pedicure bowl, foot soak and towels
Disinfected toenail clippers, cuticle pushers and nippers in a closed container
New files, orange sticks, toe separators and a pumice stone or foot file for each client
Foot cream, polish remover, base coat, colours and top coat
Disinfectant for the foot spa, made up as the maker says
Client record cards, gloves and a sharps box

The feet before the service, and the completed record card
Toenails cut straight across and filed
Hard skin being smoothed with a pumice stone or foot file
The finished polished toenails with toe separators
The foot spa drained, cleaned and disinfected
checklist: Checked the feet for contraindications and recorded the consultation
Tested the water temperature before the client's feet went in
Dried the feet well, especially between the toes
Cut the toenails straight across, not too short, and filed the edges smooth
Smoothed hard skin safely with a pumice stone or foot file, not a blade
Gave a foot massage with correct movements, avoiding any broken skin
Applied polish neatly with toe separators in place
Drained, cleaned and disinfected the foot spa as the maker says and gave aftercare advice
safety: Test water temperature before use; take extra care with clients who have diabetes
Do not treat over athlete's foot, fungal nails, cuts or swelling; refer to a doctor
Keep electrical foot spas away from spilled water and check the cable first
Wipe up water at once so nobody slips
Use single-use items once; put sharps in the sharps box
